page: Microsoft Azure D32pls_v6 is a general-purpose, low-memory virtual machine instance built on Microsoft ARM architecture. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 3.4 GHz via Microsoft Neoverse-N2 silicon, with 1 thread per core. The processor features 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside hardware AES cryptography support. Memory capacity is allocated at 64.0 GB total, delivering 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached premium storage options.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel throughput across multiple core-heavy workloads. Multi-core operations register in the upper quartile, including a stress-ng score of 66293.46 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 19970.0. Memory bandwidth exhibits exceptional metrics, reaching 449.06 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 188.51 GB/sec on large-block writes, landing in the top ten percent of evaluated instances. Synthetic transactional benchmarks also perform well, indicated by a top-tier PassMark database operations score of 38223.2 and 61.87 million Redis SET operations per second.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio presents an economical hardware profile for compute-dense tasks that do not require high memory-per-core allocations. Tradeoffs center on the absence of bundled local storage, requiring external disk configuration, and subdued performance on heavy large-language-model inference tasks where lack of specialized vector instructions or accelerators limits execution. The instance is suited for multi-threaded compilation pipelines, web serving clusters, caching tiers, and scale-out containerized microservices.
description: Microsoft Azure D32pls_v6 is an ARM-based compute instance equipped with 32 dedicated cores and 32 vCPUs powered by Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processors clocked at 3.4 GHz. Featuring a compact 1:2 memory-to-core ratio, it provides 64.0 GB of system memory backed by 128 MB of L3 cache, with no integrated local storage or GPU hardware. The platform excels in uncached memory bandwidth and multi-threaded throughput, recording top-tier results in PassMark database operations alongside high-capacity Redis throughput and solid Clang software compilation scores. Single-core benchmarks and large-model inference metrics show average-to-modest performance, reflecting the architectural emphasis on density and scale-out efficiency over extreme single-thread or AI accelerator power. The D32pls_v6 is well aligned with multi-threaded build jobs, web serving architectures, microservices, and distributed in-memory data processing tasks.
